
===== function dialoguePortraitCameraAim =====
018583:       // Cutscene dialogue's stand-in for a "player" anchor: the real
018584:       // dialoguePortraitCameraAim below hardcodes the actual player mesh as
018585:       // one of its two portrait-center anchors, which is meaningless here
018586:       // (neither cutscene speaker is ever the real player, who may be
018587:       // sitting untouched somewhere else entirely in the save). Pins the
018588:       // shot to the SPEAKING actor's own visual center instead — a
018589:       // creature's avatarRef.group already sits at its own body-center
018590:       // height (see cutscenePreviewApplyState), while an NPC/player's
018591:       // coin-plane needs the same portrait-tagged-child lookup real
018592:       // gameplay uses. Returns null (falling back to the generic elevated
018593:       // follow-camera framing) for a freeform placeholder actor, which has
018594:       // neither.
018595:       function cutscenePreviewSpeakerCenterY(entity) {
018596:         if (!entity) return null;
018597:         if (entity.kind === 'creature') return entity.root?.position.y ?? null;
018598:         return portraitAvatarCenterWorldPosition(entity.root)?.y ?? null;
018599:       }

018601:       function dialoguePortraitCameraAim(modeCfg, tx, tz, distance, baseAngle) {

018603:         if (cutscenePreviewActive) {
018604:           const y = cutscenePreviewSpeakerCenterY(cutscenePreviewDialogueSpeaker);
018605:           return y == null ? null : { cameraY: y, lookY: y, targetX: tx, targetZ: tz };
018606:         }
018607:         if (!_dialogueWalker?.root) return null;
018608:         const hasAuthoredSpeakerHead = typeof _dialogueWalker.dialogueHeadWorldPosition === 'function';
018609:         const npcCenter = hasAuthoredSpeakerHead
018610:           ? _dialogueWalker.dialogueHeadWorldPosition(new THREE.Vector3())
018611:           : portraitAvatarCenterWorldPosition(_dialogueWalker.root);
018612:         if (!npcCenter) return null;
018613: 
018614:         // Animal-shaped dialogue speakers provide an authored head point rather than
018615:         // an NPC portrait center. Treat that exact world-space pixel as the normal
018616:         // npcDialogue camera target: same configured distance/angle/azimuth/zoom,
018617:         // but no player->speaker pitch extrapolation (which can aim below terrain
018618:         // when the speaker is much shorter than the player).
018619:         if (hasAuthoredSpeakerHead) {
018620:           return {
018621:             cameraY: npcCenter.y + Math.sin(baseAngle) * distance,
018622:             lookY: npcCenter.y,
018623:             targetX: npcCenter.x,
018624:             targetZ: npcCenter.z,
018625:           };
018626:         }
018627: 
018628:         const playerCenter = portraitAvatarCenterWorldPosition(playerMesh);
018629:         if (!playerCenter) return null;
018630:         const minDistance = modeCfg.portraitCenterMinDistanceTiles ?? 0.001;
018631:         const portraitDistance = Math.max(
018632:           minDistance,
018633:           Math.hypot(npcCenter.x - playerCenter.x, npcCenter.z - playerCenter.z),
018634:         );
018635:         const rawPortraitPitch = Math.atan2(npcCenter.y - playerCenter.y, portraitDistance);

009035:       let cameraAngleOffsetDeg   = 0;

009037:       // THREE.Raycaster per call would just be needless per-frame garbage.
009038:       const _cameraOcclusionRaycaster = new THREE.Raycaster();
009039:       // Camera azimuth (radians, rotated from due-south toward east) for the active
009040:       // mode. Everything except "fishing" stays at 0 (camera due south, as before).
009041:       function activeCameraAzimuthRad() {
009042:         return THREE.MathUtils.degToRad((cameraModeConfig(activeCameraMode).azimuthDeg ?? 0) + cameraAzimuthOffsetDeg);
009043:       }
009044:       // The world direction the camera is actually looking (as opposed to
009045:       // activeCameraAzimuthRad(), which is where the camera SITS relative to
009046:       // its target) — used by shoulder-surf to make WASD relative to
009047:       // wherever the mouse has turned the camera. updateCameraPosition
009048:       // places the camera at world offset (sin(az), cos(az))*distance from
009049:       // its look-at target and then looks back at that target, so the
009050:       // camera's own view direction is the negation of that offset;
009051:       // converting (-sin(az), -cos(az)) into this game's atan2(y,x) facing
009052:       // convention (matching facingAngle/lastMoveAngle elsewhere) reduces to
009053:       // -az - 90°. Cross-checked against beginSitInteraction's "camera sits
009054:       // opposite the character's facing" azimuth (270 - facingDeg): feeding
009055:       // that back through this gives exactly facingAngle again.
009056:       function cameraFacingAngleRad() {
009057:         return angleDiff(-activeCameraAzimuthRad() - Math.PI / 2, 0);
009058:       }
009059:       // Billboard sprites go edge-on (and effectively disappear) when rotated
009060:       // perpendicular to the camera's current viewing axis. perpClamp's dead zones
009061:       // need to rotate along with the camera's azimuth so this still works once the
009062:       // camera isn't pointed due north (e.g. the "fishing" mode's diagonal framing).
009063:       function cameraRelativePerps() {
009064:         const az = activeCameraAzimuthRad();
009065:         return [Math.PI / 2 + az, -Math.PI / 2 + az];

024106:         // ── Camera smooth follow ─────────────────────────────────
024107:         const targetPosition = activeCameraTarget?.position;
024108:         const wx = targetPosition ? targetPosition.x : player.x / TILE;
024109:         const wz = targetPosition ? targetPosition.z : player.y / TILE;
024110:         // Shoulder-surf tracks the actual rendered player mesh height rather
024111:         // than bare ground height, so the camera rises and sinks along with
024112:         // it — mountSeatLift/chairSeatSink/water bob/etc. (see the movement
024113:         // update's targetY) already compose into playerMesh.position.y every
024114:         // frame before this runs, so mounting a tall creature or wading into
024115:         // water carries straight through to the camera for free.
024116:         const wy = targetPosition ? targetPosition.y
024117:           : (activeCameraMode === SHOULDER_SURF_MODE ? playerMesh.position.y : _playerGroundY());
024118:         const camLerp = cameraModeConfig(activeCameraMode).followLerp ?? 0.08;
024119:         camTargetX += (wx - camTargetX) * camLerp;
024120:         camTargetZ += (wz - camTargetZ) * camLerp;
024121:         camTargetY += (wy - camTargetY) * camLerp;
024122:         // Safety net: some camera-mode transitions (fishing, the music
024123:         // minigame, NPC dialogue, harvest interactions...) assign
024124:         // activeCameraMode directly rather than through
024125:         // enterDefaultCameraMode(), so this catches any of them landing
024126:         // outside shoulder-surf while its Pointer Lock is still held —
024127:         // cheap enough (one property read) to just check every frame rather
024128:         // than hunting down every such call site individually.
024129:         if (!cursorlessMouseAimRequested()) releaseShoulderSurfPointerLock();
024130:         // Same "don't hunt down every mode-switch call site" reasoning as
024131:         // the Pointer Lock release above — held-item ground x-ray reads as
024132:         // clarity from the normal top-down view but just looks wrong at
024133:         // shoulder-surf's close third-person range, so keep it in lockstep
024134:         // with the camera mode every frame instead.
024135:         window.HeldObjectRenderOrder?.setEnabled(activeCameraMode !== SHOULDER_SURF_MODE);
024136:         // Eases the camera's actual offset (…_current) toward whichever
024137:         // stance preset applies right now — every frame, not just the
024138:         // instant the stance flips — so drawing/sheathing a weapon (or any
024139:         // other tool/item swap that changes stance) reads as a smooth
024140:         // push-in/pull-back instead of a jump-cut. The offset sliders'
024141:         // displayed value still jumps immediately on the flip, since that's
024142:         // just showing which preset's number is now in charge, not the

028304:       // Resolves a random real-recording footstep URL for whatever surface
028305:       // this NPC is currently standing on — same surface resolution
028306:       // _tickFootsteps uses for their actual footfalls — turned into an
028307:       // absolute URL so it still loads correctly from inside the Lyre
028308:       // minigame's own iframe (a different base path under assets/minigames/).
028309:       // Used to give an ambient NPC performance's metronome a beat that
028310:       // matches the ground they're actually playing on instead of a
028311:       // generic click.
028312:       function npcFootstepSampleUrl(npcId) {
028313:         const walker = npcWalkers.find(w => w.rec?.id === npcId);
028314:         if (!walker || !window.AudioSystem) return null;
028315:         const wx = walker.root.position.x * TILE, wy = walker.root.position.z * TILE;
028316:         const tile = window.AudioSystem.footstepTileAt(walker.area, wx, wy, npcGridForArea(walker.area));
028317:         const surfaceKey = window.AudioSystem.footstepSurfaceKey(walker.area, tile?.type ?? null);
028318:         const urls = window.AudioSystem.gameAudioConfig()?.footsteps?.surfaces?.[surfaceKey]?.urls;
028319:         if (!urls?.length) return null;
028320:         const url = urls[Math.floor(Math.random() * urls.length)];
028321:         try { return new URL(url, document.baseURI).href; } catch { return url; }
028322:       }

028324:       window.MusicMinigame?.init({
028325:         refreshActionBar,
028326:         getCurrentArea: () => currentArea,
028327:         listInstrumentPerformers,
028328:         getNpcFootstepSampleUrl: npcFootstepSampleUrl,
028329:         showToast,
028330:         // Frames the performance in third-person (see the "music" camera
028331:         // mode in scratchbones-config.js) instead of leaving the default
028332:         // camera in place — matches how fishing/dialogue each get their
028333:         // own framing. In backup mode the target sits at the midpoint
028334:         // between the player and whichever NPC they joined, so both stay
028335:         // in shot; in lead/solo mode it just follows the player as usual.
028336:         beginMusicCamera: (npcId) => {
028337:           _musicPrevCameraMode = activeCameraMode;
028338:           _musicPrevCameraTarget = activeCameraTarget;
028339:           activeCameraMode = 'music';
028340:           const walker = npcId ? npcWalkers.find(w => w.rec?.id === npcId) : null;
028341:           if (walker?.root) {
028342:             const midX = (player.x / TILE + walker.root.position.x) / 2;
028343:             const midZ = (player.y / TILE + walker.root.position.z) / 2;
028344:             activeCameraTarget = { position: new THREE.Vector3(midX, 0, midZ) };
028345:           } else {
028346:             activeCameraTarget = null;
028347:           }
028348:         },
028349:         endMusicCamera: () => {
028350:           activeCameraMode = _musicPrevCameraMode ?? 'default';
028351:           activeCameraTarget = _musicPrevCameraTarget ?? null;
028352:           _musicPrevCameraMode = null;
028353:           _musicPrevCameraTarget = null;
028354:         },
028355:         // Driven by js/music-minigame.js's 'sounded-note' relay from either
028356:         // the player's overlay iframe or an NPC's ambient performance iframe
028357:         // — see updateHeldItemHolder (player) and the station-tool block
028358:         // above (NPC) for what actually owns each twitch state.
028359:         triggerPlayerKurrayaTwitch: () => {
028360:           if (_heldItemPlane?.userData.kurrayaAssembly) triggerKurrayaTwitch(_playerKurrayaTwitch, _heldItemPlane);
028361:         },
028362:         triggerNpcKurrayaTwitch: (npcId) => {
028363:           const walker = npcId ? npcWalkers.find(w => w.rec?.id === npcId) : null;
028364:           if (walker?.stationToolMesh?.userData.kurrayaAssembly) triggerKurrayaTwitch(walker.stationKurrayaTwitch, walker.stationToolMesh);
028365:         },
028366:       });

029916:       //  handoff script in index.html, just before <script src="game.js">,
029917:       //  and docs/tools/cutscene-director/index.html's "Preview in game"
029918:       //  button) instead of the real save, and replays an authored
029919:       //  cutscene using the REAL dialogue UI and REAL dialogue-zoom camera
029920:       //  system — not the Director tool's own private preview.
029921:       //
029922:       //  The differences from a normal conversation are deliberate and
029923:       //  narrow, and live right next to the code they change:
029924:       //    - beginNpcDialogueStaging / faceNpcDialogueParticipants /
029925:       //      updateNpcDialogueStaging (above) no-op when
029926:       //      cutscenePreviewActive — the director already scripts every
029927:       //      participant's exact position/facing frame by frame, so the
029928:       //      real "walk the player up to the NPC" auto-staging would only
029929:       //      fight it, and there may not even be a "player" among the
029930:       //      scene's actors.
029931:       //    - advanceNpcDialogue (above) delegates to
029932:       //      cutscenePreviewAdvance — the director walks its own
029933:       //      move/talk/choice/... stage list, not an authored dialogueTree.
029934:       //    - Camera/dialogue-zoom targeting reuses activeCameraTarget
029935:       //      exactly as normal NPC dialogue already does (openNpcDialogue
029936:       //      sets it to walker.root) — it's just pointed at whichever
029937:       //      cutscene participant is currently speaking instead of always
029938:       //      being "the NPC the player walked up to." That target is never
029939:       //      the real singleton player/playerMesh, even for a "Player"
029940:       //      role actor in the scene — every actor, including that one, is
029941:       //      spawned as its own independent stand-in entity here, so this
029942:       //      previewer never reads or writes the real player's position.
029943:       //      The real player sits exactly wherever their save left them,
029944:       //      off-screen and untouched, for the whole preview.

030523:         function continueTo(nextId) {
030524:           if (!running) return;
030525:           if (dialogueOpen) closeLine();
030526:           if (!nextId) { finish(); return; }
030527:           runStage(nextId);
030528:         }
030529: 
030530:         function runStage(stageId) {
030531:           if (!running) return;
030532:           const stage = stagesById.get(stageId);
030533:           if (!stage) { finish('Preview stopped — the next card could not be found.'); return; }
030534:           cutscenePreviewBanner(`🎬 ${payload.title || 'Cutscene'} — ${stage.type}`, false);
030535: 
030536:           if (stage.type === 'move') return runMove(stage);
030537:           if (stage.type === 'animation') return runAnimation(stage);
030538:           if (stage.type === 'turn') return runTurn(stage);
030539:           if (stage.type === 'combat') return runCombat(stage);
030540:           if (stage.type === 'fade') return runFade(stage);
030541:           if (stage.type === 'zoom') return runZoom(stage);

===== function npcDialogueCameraMode =====
010317:       // faces" derivation beginSitInteraction uses for the seated camera's
010318:       // initial framing. From here on, plain mouse movement (see the
010319:       // mousemove handler's freeRotate branch) drives cameraAzimuthOffsetDeg
010320:       // directly — this only ever runs once per mode-entry, not continuously.
010321:       function snapShoulderSurfAzimuth() {
010322:         cameraAzimuthOffsetDeg = wrapAzimuthDeg(270 - facingAngle * 180 / Math.PI - (cameraModeConfig(SHOULDER_SURF_MODE).azimuthDeg ?? 0));
010323:         cameraAngleOffsetDeg = 0;
010324:       }
010325:       // Every call site that resolves "return to the ordinary gameplay
010326:       // camera" (dialogue close, standing up from a chair, cutscene end)
010327:       // should go through this instead of assigning defaultCameraModeKey()
010328:       // directly, so landing back in shoulder-surf always re-centers behind
010329:       // the player rather than resuming wherever a prior free-look drag left
010330:       // the azimuth.
010331:       function enterDefaultCameraMode(prevMode) {
010332:         activeCameraMode = prevMode ?? defaultCameraModeKey();
010333:         if (activeCameraMode === SHOULDER_SURF_MODE) snapShoulderSurfAzimuth();
010334:       }
010335:       function npcDialogueCameraMode() { return cameraConfig().dialogueMode || 'npcDialogue'; }
010336:       function dialogueZoomConfig() { return cameraModeConfig(npcDialogueCameraMode()).runtimeZoom || {}; }
010337:       function dialogueZoomEnabled() { return dialogueZoomConfig().enabled !== false; }
010338:       function dialogueZoomActive() { return dialogueOpen && activeCameraMode === npcDialogueCameraMode() && dialogueZoomEnabled(); }
010339:       function clampDialogueZoomPercent(value) {
010340:         const cfg = dialogueZoomConfig();
010341:         return clamp(value, cfg.minPercent ?? 0, cfg.maxPercent ?? 100);
010342:       }
010343:       function dialogueZoomFactor() {
010344:         const cfg = dialogueZoomConfig();
010345:         const minPercent = cfg.minPercent ?? 0;
010346:         const maxPercent = cfg.maxPercent ?? 100;
010347:         const range = Math.max(0.001, maxPercent - minPercent);
010348:         const normalized = clamp((dialogueCameraZoomPercent - minPercent) / range, 0, 1);
010349:         return 1 + normalized * ((cfg.maxZoomFactor ?? 2.5) - 1);
010350:       }
010351:       function setDialogueCameraZoomPercent(value) {
010352:         dialogueCameraZoomPercent = clampDialogueZoomPercent(value);
010353:         updateDialogueZoomIndicator();
010354:       }
010355:       function updateDialogueZoomIndicator() {
010356:         if (!dialogueZoomIndicator) return;
010357:         dialogueZoomIndicator.textContent = `${Math.round(dialogueCameraZoomPercent)}%`;
010358:         dialogueZoomIndicator.setAttribute('aria-hidden', dialogueZoomActive() ? 'false' : 'true');
010359:         dialogueZoomIndicator.classList.toggle('open', dialogueZoomActive());
010360:       }
010361:       function resetDialogueCameraZoom() {
010362:         setDialogueCameraZoomPercent(dialogueZoomConfig().initialPercent ?? 0);
010363:       }
010364:       function desktopControlsConfig() { return window.SCRATCHBONES_CONFIG?.game?.desktopControls || {}; }
010365:       function npcDialogueButtonConfig() {
010366:         return window.SCRATCHBONES_CONFIG?.game?.mobileControls?.npcDialogueButton || {};
010367:       }
010368:       function npcDialogueAction() { return npcDialogueButtonConfig().action || 'npc_dialogue'; }

010343:       function dialogueZoomFactor() {
010344:         const cfg = dialogueZoomConfig();

010346:         const maxPercent = cfg.maxPercent ?? 100;
010347:         const range = Math.max(0.001, maxPercent - minPercent);
010348:         const normalized = clamp((dialogueCameraZoomPercent - minPercent) / range, 0, 1);
010349:         return 1 + normalized * ((cfg.maxZoomFactor ?? 2.5) - 1);
010350:       }

018913:         // — the same over-the-shoulder framing knobs most third-person games
018914:         // expose — so they stay "camera-left/right" and "higher/lower"
018915:         // regardless of which way the head/camera currently points. Shifting
018916:         // the look-at point here (rather than the final camera position
018917:         // directly) carries the offset into idealX/idealZ/cameraY below too,
018918:         // sliding the whole camera rig rather than just skewing its aim.
018919:         if (activeCameraMode === SHOULDER_SURF_MODE && !portraitAim) {
018920:           const rightX = Math.cos(azimuth), rightZ = -Math.sin(azimuth);
018921:           lookAtX += rightX * s_shoulderSurfOffsetH_current;
018922:           lookAtZ += rightZ * s_shoulderSurfOffsetH_current;
018923:           lookY += s_shoulderSurfOffsetV_current;
018924:         }
018925:         const cameraY = portraitAim?.cameraY ?? (lookY + Math.sin(angle) * distance);
018926:         const groundDistance = Math.cos(angle) * distance;
018927:         const idealX = lookAtX + Math.sin(azimuth) * groundDistance;
018928:         const idealZ = lookAtZ + Math.cos(azimuth) * groundDistance; // +Z = south
018929:         const safe = occlusionSafeCameraPosition(lookAtX, lookY, lookAtZ, idealX, cameraY, idealZ);
018930:         camera.position.set(safe.x, safe.y, safe.z);
018931:         camera.lookAt(lookAtX, lookY, lookAtZ);
018932:         camera.fov = modeCfg.fovDeg ?? 42;
018933:         camera.aspect = threeContainer.clientWidth / threeContainer.clientHeight;
018934:         camera.updateProjectionMatrix();
018935:       }

018904:         const azimuth = THREE.MathUtils.degToRad((modeCfg.azimuthDeg ?? 0) + cameraAzimuthOffsetDeg);
018905:         const portraitAim = dialoguePortraitCameraAim(modeCfg, tx, tz, distance, angle);
018906:         let lookY = portraitAim?.lookY ?? (camTargetY + (modeCfg.targetYOffsetTiles ?? 0));
018907:         // Camera sits at `azimuth` east of due-south from the target, elevated,
018908:         // looking back at it. azimuth=0 (every mode but "fishing") reduces to the
018909:         // original due-south-looking-north framing.
018910:         let lookAtX = portraitAim?.targetX ?? tx, lookAtZ = portraitAim?.targetZ ?? tz;
018911:         // Shoulder-surf's horizontal/vertical camera-offset sliders (Settings
018912:         // → Camera), applied relative to the camera's own right/world-up axes
018913:         // — the same over-the-shoulder framing knobs most third-person games
018914:         // expose — so they stay "camera-left/right" and "higher/lower"
018915:         // regardless of which way the head/camera currently points. Shifting
018916:         // the look-at point here (rather than the final camera position
018917:         // directly) carries the offset into idealX/idealZ/cameraY below too,
018918:         // sliding the whole camera rig rather than just skewing its aim.
018919:         if (activeCameraMode === SHOULDER_SURF_MODE && !portraitAim) {
018920:           const rightX = Math.cos(azimuth), rightZ = -Math.sin(azimuth);
018921:           lookAtX += rightX * s_shoulderSurfOffsetH_current;
018922:           lookAtZ += rightZ * s_shoulderSurfOffsetH_current;
018923:           lookY += s_shoulderSurfOffsetV_current;
018924:         }
018925:         const cameraY = portraitAim?.cameraY ?? (lookY + Math.sin(angle) * distance);
018926:         const groundDistance = Math.cos(angle) * distance;
018927:         const idealX = lookAtX + Math.sin(azimuth) * groundDistance;
018928:         const idealZ = lookAtZ + Math.cos(azimuth) * groundDistance; // +Z = south
018929:         const safe = occlusionSafeCameraPosition(lookAtX, lookY, lookAtZ, idealX, cameraY, idealZ);
018930:         camera.position.set(safe.x, safe.y, safe.z);
018931:         camera.lookAt(lookAtX, lookY, lookAtZ);
018932:         camera.fov = modeCfg.fovDeg ?? 42;
018933:         camera.aspect = threeContainer.clientWidth / threeContainer.clientHeight;
018934:         camera.updateProjectionMatrix();
018935:       }

018939:       // the standalone foliage tool's updateForestGeometryCulling. Toggling

018657:       // instead, same as town/farm below. Town and farm buildings, and any
-----
018844:             resultX = lookAtX + dx * t;
018845:             resultY = lookAtY + dy * t;
018846:             resultZ = lookAtZ + dz * t;
018847:           } else {
018848:             resultY = minCameraY;
018849:           }
018850:         }
018851:         return { x: resultX, y: resultY, z: resultZ };

018853: 
018854:       // How far under a tree canopy's own recorded influence radius the player
018855:       // has to be before manual zoom-out gets hard-limited to its underside
018856:       // height — ports the standalone foliage tool's camera-vs-canopy
018857:       // obstruction concept (see buildZoneScene's canopyZones / the
018858:       // vegGroup.userData.canopyClamp tagging in _buildZoneFloorMeshes).
018859:       // Only ever raises the effective zoom used for THIS frame's distance —
018860:       // never mutates s_zoomScale itself, so the player's own wheel/slider
018861:       // setting is restored the instant they step out of every canopy's radius.
018862:       function canopyZoomFloor(tx, tz, lookY) {
018863:         if (!_isZoneArea(currentArea)) return 0;
018864:         const zones = _zoneScenes.get(currentArea)?.canopyZones;
018865:         if (!zones || !zones.length) return 0;
018866:         const modeCfg = cameraModeConfig(activeCameraMode);
018867:         const angle = THREE.MathUtils.degToRad((modeCfg.angleFromGroundDeg ?? 32.73) + cameraAngleOffsetDeg);
018868:         const distanceTiles = modeCfg.distanceTiles ?? 14;
018869:         const sinAngle = Math.sin(angle);
018870:         const CANOPY_CLEARANCE = 0.3;
018871:         let floor = 0;
018872:         for (const z of zones) {
018873:           const dx = tx - z.x, dz = tz - z.z;
018874:           if (dx * dx + dz * dz > z.radius * z.radius) continue;
018875:           const headroom = z.undersideY - CANOPY_CLEARANCE - lookY;
018876:           const required = headroom > 1e-4 ? (sinAngle * distanceTiles) / headroom : Infinity;
018877:           if (required > floor) floor = required;
018878:         }
018879:         return floor;
018880:       }
018881:       function updateCameraPosition() {
018882:         const modeCfg = cameraModeConfig(activeCameraMode);
018883:         // A cutscene Zoom card's percent (100 = the captured shot's own
018884:         // unmodified framing, higher = closer) — entirely separate from the
018885:         // player's own s_zoomScale wheel setting so it never leaks into
018886:         // normal gameplay once the cutscene ends (see cutscenePreviewZoomPercent).
018887:         const cutsceneZoomMul = cutscenePreviewActive ? 100 / (cutscenePreviewZoomPercent || 100) : 1;
018888:         const tx = camTargetX, tz = camTargetZ;
018889:         // Cutscene/dialogue/portrait framing is deliberately scripted — only
018890:         // clamp the ordinary gameplay camera against tree canopies.
018891:         let effectiveZoomScale = s_zoomScale;
018892:         if (!cutscenePreviewActive && !dialogueZoomActive()) {
018893:           const approxLookY = camTargetY + (modeCfg.targetYOffsetTiles ?? 0);
018894:           const floor = canopyZoomFloor(tx, tz, approxLookY);
018895:           if (floor > effectiveZoomScale) {
018896:             const cfg = desktopControlsConfig();
018897:             const max = Number.isFinite(Number(cfg.wheelZoomMax)) ? Number(cfg.wheelZoomMax) : 2.5;

018881:       function updateCameraPosition() {
018882:         const modeCfg = cameraModeConfig(activeCameraMode);
018883:         // A cutscene Zoom card's percent (100 = the captured shot's own
018884:         // unmodified framing, higher = closer) — entirely separate from the
018885:         // player's own s_zoomScale wheel setting so it never leaks into
018886:         // normal gameplay once the cutscene ends (see cutscenePreviewZoomPercent).
018887:         const cutsceneZoomMul = cutscenePreviewActive ? 100 / (cutscenePreviewZoomPercent || 100) : 1;
018888:         const tx = camTargetX, tz = camTargetZ;
018889:         // Cutscene/dialogue/portrait framing is deliberately scripted — only
018890:         // clamp the ordinary gameplay camera against tree canopies.
018891:         let effectiveZoomScale = s_zoomScale;
018892:         if (!cutscenePreviewActive && !dialogueZoomActive()) {
018893:           const approxLookY = camTargetY + (modeCfg.targetYOffsetTiles ?? 0);
018894:           const floor = canopyZoomFloor(tx, tz, approxLookY);
018895:           if (floor > effectiveZoomScale) {
018896:             const cfg = desktopControlsConfig();
018897:             const max = Number.isFinite(Number(cfg.wheelZoomMax)) ? Number(cfg.wheelZoomMax) : 2.5;
018898:             effectiveZoomScale = Math.min(floor, max);
018899:           }
018900:         }
018901:         const baseDistance = (modeCfg.distanceTiles ?? 14) / effectiveZoomScale * cutsceneZoomMul;
018902:         const distance = dialogueZoomActive() ? baseDistance / dialogueZoomFactor() : baseDistance;
018903:         const angle = THREE.MathUtils.degToRad((modeCfg.angleFromGroundDeg ?? 32.73) + cameraAngleOffsetDeg);
018904:         const azimuth = THREE.MathUtils.degToRad((modeCfg.azimuthDeg ?? 0) + cameraAzimuthOffsetDeg);
018905:         const portraitAim = dialoguePortraitCameraAim(modeCfg, tx, tz, distance, angle);
018906:         let lookY = portraitAim?.lookY ?? (camTargetY + (modeCfg.targetYOffsetTiles ?? 0));
018907:         // Camera sits at `azimuth` east of due-south from the target, elevated,
018908:         // looking back at it. azimuth=0 (every mode but "fishing") reduces to the
018909:         // original due-south-looking-north framing.
018910:         let lookAtX = portraitAim?.targetX ?? tx, lookAtZ = portraitAim?.targetZ ?? tz;
-----
018888:         const tx = camTargetX, tz = camTargetZ;
018889:         // Cutscene/dialogue/portrait framing is deliberately scripted — only
018890:         // clamp the ordinary gameplay camera against tree canopies.
018891:         let effectiveZoomScale = s_zoomScale;
018892:         if (!cutscenePreviewActive && !dialogueZoomActive()) {
018893:           const approxLookY = camTargetY + (modeCfg.targetYOffsetTiles ?? 0);
018894:           const floor = canopyZoomFloor(tx, tz, approxLookY);
018895:           if (floor > effectiveZoomScale) {
018896:             const cfg = desktopControlsConfig();
018897:             const max = Number.isFinite(Number(cfg.wheelZoomMax)) ? Number(cfg.wheelZoomMax) : 2.5;
018898:             effectiveZoomScale = Math.min(floor, max);
018899:           }
018900:         }
018901:         const baseDistance = (modeCfg.distanceTiles ?? 14) / effectiveZoomScale * cutsceneZoomMul;
018902:         const distance = dialogueZoomActive() ? baseDistance / dialogueZoomFactor() : baseDistance;
018903:         const angle = THREE.MathUtils.degToRad((modeCfg.angleFromGroundDeg ?? 32.73) + cameraAngleOffsetDeg);
018904:         const azimuth = THREE.MathUtils.degToRad((modeCfg.azimuthDeg ?? 0) + cameraAzimuthOffsetDeg);
018905:         const portraitAim = dialoguePortraitCameraAim(modeCfg, tx, tz, distance, angle);
018906:         let lookY = portraitAim?.lookY ?? (camTargetY + (modeCfg.targetYOffsetTiles ?? 0));
018907:         // Camera sits at `azimuth` east of due-south from the target, elevated,
018908:         // looking back at it. azimuth=0 (every mode but "fishing") reduces to the
018909:         // original due-south-looking-north framing.
018910:         let lookAtX = portraitAim?.targetX ?? tx, lookAtZ = portraitAim?.targetZ ?? tz;
018911:         // Shoulder-surf's horizontal/vertical camera-offset sliders (Settings
018912:         // → Camera), applied relative to the camera's own right/world-up axes
018913:         // — the same over-the-shoulder framing knobs most third-person games
018914:         // expose — so they stay "camera-left/right" and "higher/lower"
018915:         // regardless of which way the head/camera currently points. Shifting
018916:         // the look-at point here (rather than the final camera position
018917:         // directly) carries the offset into idealX/idealZ/cameraY below too,
018918:         // sliding the whole camera rig rather than just skewing its aim.
018919:         if (activeCameraMode === SHOULDER_SURF_MODE && !portraitAim) {
018920:           const rightX = Math.cos(azimuth), rightZ = -Math.sin(azimuth);
018921:           lookAtX += rightX * s_shoulderSurfOffsetH_current;
018922:           lookAtZ += rightZ * s_shoulderSurfOffsetH_current;
018923:           lookY += s_shoulderSurfOffsetV_current;
018924:         }
018925:         const cameraY = portraitAim?.cameraY ?? (lookY + Math.sin(angle) * distance);
018926:         const groundDistance = Math.cos(angle) * distance;
018927:         const idealX = lookAtX + Math.sin(azimuth) * groundDistance;
018928:         const idealZ = lookAtZ + Math.cos(azimuth) * groundDistance; // +Z = south
018929:         const safe = occlusionSafeCameraPosition(lookAtX, lookY, lookAtZ, idealX, cameraY, idealZ);
018930:         camera.position.set(safe.x, safe.y, safe.z);
018931:         camera.lookAt(lookAtX, lookY, lookAtZ);
018932:         camera.fov = modeCfg.fovDeg ?? 42;
018933:         camera.aspect = threeContainer.clientWidth / threeContainer.clientHeight;
018934:         camera.updateProjectionMatrix();
018935:       }

001897:       function awardToolMasteryXp(itemKey, amount) {
001898:         if (!itemKey || !TOOL_ITEM_DEFS[itemKey] || !(amount > 0) || !gearInventory) return;
001899:         if (!gearInventory.toolMastery[itemKey]) gearInventory.toolMastery[itemKey] = { xp: 0 };
001900:         gearInventory.toolMastery[itemKey].xp += amount;
001901:         window.WorldPopupText?.queueReward('masteryXp', `+${amount} ${TOOL_ITEM_DEFS[itemKey].label} Mastery`);
001902:         saveGearInventory();
001903:       }
001904: 
001905:       // Dev-mode-only test shortcut (see the "+1 Mastery" button in
001906:       // selectGearTool/selectEquipSlot, gated by s_devMode) — jumps straight
001907:       // to the XP threshold for the next level instead of adding an
001908:       // arbitrary XP amount that might not actually cross it.
001909:       function devBumpToolMasteryLevel(itemKey) {
001910:         if (!itemKey || !TOOL_ITEM_DEFS[itemKey] || !gearInventory) return;
001911:         const level = toolMasteryLevel(itemKey);
001912:         if (level >= MASTERY_XP_THRESHOLDS.length) return; // already maxed
001913:         const targetXp = MASTERY_XP_THRESHOLDS[level];
001914:         if (!gearInventory.toolMastery[itemKey]) gearInventory.toolMastery[itemKey] = { xp: 0 };
001915:         gearInventory.toolMastery[itemKey].xp = Math.max(gearInventory.toolMastery[itemKey].xp, targetXp);
001916:         saveGearInventory();
001917:       }

001921:       // equipped as the weapon.
001922:       function awardWeaponMasteryXp() {
001923:         awardToolMasteryXp(equipmentSlots.weapon, MASTERY_XP_PER_COMBAT_HIT);
001924:       }

001934:       // LEVEL) — 0% verdigris at 0 XP, 100% ("maximum verdigris") exactly
001935:       // at the mastery-5 threshold, same MASTERY_XP_THRESHOLDS toolMasteryLevel
001936:       // already reads. Only meaningful for a smith-crafted verdigris tool
001937:       // (TOOL_ITEM_DEFS[itemKey].metalKey set) — anything else reads as 0.
001938:       function toolVerdigrisFraction(itemKey) {
001939:         if (!TOOL_ITEM_DEFS[itemKey]?.metalKey) return 0;
001940:         const maxXp = MASTERY_XP_THRESHOLDS[MASTERY_XP_THRESHOLDS.length - 1];
001941:         return Math.max(0, Math.min(1, toolMasteryXp(itemKey) / maxXp));
001942:       }

003823:           // Seat surface tilt (pitch/roll only) and footprint depth, passed
003824:           // through to the leg rig's faithful surface-flush seated solve
003825:           // (see procedural-leg-animation.js's applySeatedPose). Read
003826:           // straight off the anchor's own local rotation with no further
003827:           // rotation applied for rotYDeg. Yaw is already represented by
003828:           // facingRad; the leg solver consumes seat-local pitch/roll.

003835:       function beginSitInteraction(furnitureKey, col, row, fw, fd, rotYDeg, seatIndex) {
003836:         if (sitInteraction || window.FarmAnimals.isHarvesting() || dialogueOpen || (window.Mounts?.rideState ?? 'none') !== 'none') return { ok: false, message: 'Cannot sit right now.' };
003837:         const seat = resolveSeatWorldTransform(furnitureKey, col, row, fw, fd, rotYDeg, seatIndex);
003838:         if (!seat) return { ok: false, message: 'Nowhere to sit there.' };
003839:         const seatSurfaceY = activeSurfaceYAtWorld(seat.x, seat.z); // Used to lift the seated camera with zone plateau/ramp terrain.
003840:         const seatAbsoluteWorldY = seatSurfaceY + seat.y; // Used only by world-space camera/debug consumers; seat.y stays floor-relative for anatomy.
003841:         const targetX = seat.x * TILE, targetY = seat.z * TILE;
003842:         const targetAngle = seat.facingRad;
003843:         sitInteraction = {
003844:           furnitureKey, col, row,
003845:           phase: 'in', t: 0,
003846:           startX: player.x, startY: player.y, startAngle: facingAngle,
003847:           targetX, targetY, targetAngle,
003848:           seatWorldY: seat.y,
003849:           seatSurfaceY,
003850:           seatAbsoluteWorldY,
003851:           seatNormalDeg: seat.normalDeg,
003852:           seatFootprintHalfDepth: seat.footprintHalfDepth,
003853:           seatAnchorZ: seat.anchorZ,
003854:           prevCameraMode: activeCameraMode, prevCameraTarget: activeCameraTarget,
003855:         };
003856:         activeCameraMode = 'seated';
003857:         activeCameraTarget = { position: new THREE.Vector3(seat.x, seatAbsoluteWorldY + 0.15, seat.z) };
003858:         // Start looking at the seated character's BACK rather than whatever
003859:         // the 'seated' mode's base azimuth happens to be (which has no
003860:         // relationship to which way the character is actually facing).
003861:         // updateCameraPosition's own azimuth convention: azimuth=0 sits the
003862:         // camera due south of the target looking north (see its comment);
003863:         // targetAngle is in the atan2(z,x) convention facingAngle/player.angle
003864:         // use elsewhere (0 = +X), so the world direction the character is
003865:         // FACING is (cos(targetAngle), sin(targetAngle)) in (X,Z) — camera
003866:         // needs to sit on the OPPOSITE side (the character's back), i.e. at
003867:         // world azimuth atan2(-cos(targetAngle), -sin(targetAngle)), which
003868:         // simplifies to 270° − targetAngle(deg).
003869:         const behindAzimuthDeg = 270 - targetAngle * 180 / Math.PI;
003870:         cameraAzimuthOffsetDeg = wrapAzimuthDeg(behindAzimuthDeg - (cameraModeConfig('seated').azimuthDeg ?? 0));
003871:         cameraAngleOffsetDeg = 0;
003872:         return { ok: true, message: 'You sit down.' };
003873:       }

003875:       function endSitInteraction() {
003876:         if (!sitInteraction || sitInteraction.phase === 'out') return;
-----
003829:           normalDeg: { x: anchor.rotationDeg.x || 0, z: anchor.rotationDeg.z || 0 },
003830:           footprintHalfDepth: Math.max(0.05, (Number(data.footprint?.d) || 1) / 2),
003831:           anchorZ: az,
003832:         };
003833:       }

003835:       function beginSitInteraction(furnitureKey, col, row, fw, fd, rotYDeg, seatIndex) {
003836:         if (sitInteraction || window.FarmAnimals.isHarvesting() || dialogueOpen || (window.Mounts?.rideState ?? 'none') !== 'none') return { ok: false, message: 'Cannot sit right now.' };
003837:         const seat = resolveSeatWorldTransform(furnitureKey, col, row, fw, fd, rotYDeg, seatIndex);
003838:         if (!seat) return { ok: false, message: 'Nowhere to sit there.' };
003839:         const seatSurfaceY = activeSurfaceYAtWorld(seat.x, seat.z); // Used to lift the seated camera with zone plateau/ramp terrain.
003840:         const seatAbsoluteWorldY = seatSurfaceY + seat.y; // Used only by world-space camera/debug consumers; seat.y stays floor-relative for anatomy.
003841:         const targetX = seat.x * TILE, targetY = seat.z * TILE;
003842:         const targetAngle = seat.facingRad;
003843:         sitInteraction = {
003844:           furnitureKey, col, row,
003845:           phase: 'in', t: 0,
003846:           startX: player.x, startY: player.y, startAngle: facingAngle,
003847:           targetX, targetY, targetAngle,
003848:           seatWorldY: seat.y,
003849:           seatSurfaceY,
003850:           seatAbsoluteWorldY,
003851:           seatNormalDeg: seat.normalDeg,
003852:           seatFootprintHalfDepth: seat.footprintHalfDepth,
003853:           seatAnchorZ: seat.anchorZ,
003854:           prevCameraMode: activeCameraMode, prevCameraTarget: activeCameraTarget,
003855:         };
003856:         activeCameraMode = 'seated';
003857:         activeCameraTarget = { position: new THREE.Vector3(seat.x, seatAbsoluteWorldY + 0.15, seat.z) };
003858:         // Start looking at the seated character's BACK rather than whatever
003859:         // the 'seated' mode's base azimuth happens to be (which has no
003860:         // relationship to which way the character is actually facing).
003861:         // updateCameraPosition's own azimuth convention: azimuth=0 sits the
003862:         // camera due south of the target looking north (see its comment);
003863:         // targetAngle is in the atan2(z,x) convention facingAngle/player.angle
003864:         // use elsewhere (0 = +X), so the world direction the character is
003865:         // FACING is (cos(targetAngle), sin(targetAngle)) in (X,Z) — camera
003866:         // needs to sit on the OPPOSITE side (the character's back), i.e. at
003867:         // world azimuth atan2(-cos(targetAngle), -sin(targetAngle)), which
003868:         // simplifies to 270° − targetAngle(deg).
003869:         const behindAzimuthDeg = 270 - targetAngle * 180 / Math.PI;
003870:         cameraAzimuthOffsetDeg = wrapAzimuthDeg(behindAzimuthDeg - (cameraModeConfig('seated').azimuthDeg ?? 0));
003871:         cameraAngleOffsetDeg = 0;
003872:         return { ok: true, message: 'You sit down.' };
003873:       }
003874: 
003875:       function endSitInteraction() {
003876:         if (!sitInteraction || sitInteraction.phase === 'out') return;
003877:         sitInteraction.phase = 'out';
003878:         sitInteraction.t = 0;
003879:       }

003881:       function updateSitInteraction(dt) {
003882:         const s = sitInteraction;
-----
003891:           // the instant you sit down. Same keyboard-wins-over-joystick
003892:           // source selection as the normal movement read just above in the
003893:           // main update loop. Sign matches the mouse-drag azimuth control
003894:           // (dragging/looking right also decreases the offset).
003895:           const kb = getKeyboardVector();
003896:           const ix = kb.active ? kb.x : input.x;
003897:           const iy = kb.active ? kb.y : input.y;
003898:           if (Math.abs(ix) > 0.001) {
003899:             cameraAzimuthOffsetDeg = wrapAzimuthDeg(cameraAzimuthOffsetDeg - ix * SEATED_LOOK_ROTATE_DEG_PER_SEC * dt);
003900:           }
003901:           if (Math.abs(iy) > 0.001) {
003902:             cameraAngleOffsetDeg = clamp(cameraAngleOffsetDeg + iy * SEATED_LOOK_ROTATE_DEG_PER_SEC * dt, -SEATED_CAMERA_PITCH_CLAMP_DEG, SEATED_CAMERA_PITCH_CLAMP_DEG);
003903:           }
003904:           return;
003905:         }
003906:         s.t = Math.min(1, s.t + dt / SIT_TRANSITION_S);
003907:         const e = s.t;
003908:         const [fromX, fromY, fromAngle, toX, toY, toAngle] = s.phase === 'in'
003909:           ? [s.startX, s.startY, s.startAngle, s.targetX, s.targetY, s.targetAngle]
003910:           : [s.targetX, s.targetY, s.targetAngle, s.startX, s.startY, s.startAngle];
003911:         player.x = fromX + (toX - fromX) * e;
003912:         player.y = fromY + (toY - fromY) * e;
003913:         facingAngle = fromAngle + angleDiff(toAngle, fromAngle) * e;
003914:         player.angle = facingAngle;
003915:         if (e >= 1) {
003916:           if (s.phase === 'in') { s.phase = 'active'; s.t = 0; }
003917:           else {
003918:             enterDefaultCameraMode(s.prevCameraMode);
003919:             activeCameraTarget = s.prevCameraTarget ?? null;
003920:             // enterDefaultCameraMode already snapped these behind the player
003921:             // when landing back in shoulder-surf — don't stomp that back to
003922:             // due-south here too.
003923:             if (activeCameraMode !== SHOULDER_SURF_MODE) {
003924:               cameraAzimuthOffsetDeg = 0;
003925:               cameraAngleOffsetDeg = 0;
003926:             }
003927:             sitInteraction = null;
003928:           }
003929:         }
003930:       }

003935:       // own bodyYaw flourish; this local neck residual counters both. Seated
003936:       // free-look treats the orbited camera direction as the aim target.

006448:       function _playerFaceTarget(master = player) {
006449:         const isPlayer = master === player;
006450:         const pos = isPlayer
006451:           ? window.CreatureHeadCache.getHeadWorld(player, 'player', { x: player.x, y: player.y, mesh: playerMesh, avatarModelHeight: playerAvatarModelHeight })
006452:           : window.CreatureHeadCache.getHeadWorld(master, 'companion-portrait');
006453:         return { x: pos.x, y: pos.z, worldY: pos.worldY };
006454:       }

006473:       function _updateCreatureLookAtFace(c, master, dt) {
006474:         const target = _playerFaceTarget(master);
006475:         const dx = target.x - c.x, dy = target.y - c.y;
006476:         const horizontalPx = Math.hypot(dx, dy);
006477:         const aimAngle = horizontalPx > 1 ? Math.atan2(dy, dx) : (c.facing || 0);
006478:         const horizontalWorld = Math.max(0.15, horizontalPx / TILE);
006479:         // Negated — this rig's own convention is negative degrees = up,
006480:         // positive = down (confirmed via the vocalization head-nod, see
006481:         // png-plane-avatar.js's applyDegrees), the opposite of what a
006482:         // plain atan2 of the vertical delta gives.
006483:         const pitchDeg = -Math.atan2(target.worldY - _creatureHeadWorldY(c), horizontalWorld) * 180 / Math.PI;
006484:         _updateCompanionHeadRotation(c, pitchDeg, dt);
006485:         _setLookAtDebug(c, target.x, target.y, target.worldY);
006486:         return aimAngle;
006487:       }

006489:       // Where a living thing's "head" is, in the raw-px + worldY convention
006490:       // _updateCreatureHeadLookAtCombatTarget/companion horizon-scan both
006491:       // use (see below). The player has a real authored face height
006492:       // (_playerFaceTarget); an NPC walker has the same eye-position math
006493:       // dialogue's eye contact uses (_dialogueEyeWorldPosition), just
006494:       // converted out of its native tile-scale units into this function's
006495:       // raw-px convention; any other creature (patrol-chase predator/prey,
006496:       // a horizon-scan lock) doesn't carry anything that precise, so its
006497:       // head is approximated as its own head-rig pivot's height, nudged 5%
006498:       // of its own sprite width toward its face/snout (the authored sprites
006499:       // all face the same "front" edge of their own local frame) rather

006945: 
006946:       // The player's own avatar planes and a companion's are both flat,
006947:       // alphaTest-cutout billboards — at this camera's oblique ~33°-
006948:       // elevation angle they're genuinely tilted relative to it, so their
006949:       // real 3D depth spans overlap across their own width and height
006950:       // (confirmed live: even at the camera's default azimuth, the
006951:       // player's own plane corners alone span a wider depth range than a
006952:       // typical companion-to-player gap). A plain depth test then
006953:       // interleaves them pixel-by-pixel instead of cleanly ordering one in
006954:       // front of the other. A companion genuinely walks anywhere relative
006955:       // to the player (unlike a shoulder pet, always glued to the same
006956:       // authored offset), so there's no fixed "always in front" rule that
006957:       // would look right in every situation — this has to stay a live,
006958:       // every-frame real-camera-space-distance ranking. depthTest stays on
006959:       // for both, so real-world occlusion (trees, buildings) is untouched
006960:       // — opaque world geometry already finishes its own depth-writing
006961:       // pass before either avatar (both transparent:true) ever draws, so
006962:       // this only ever affects the two of them relative to each other.
006963:       const _depthPriorityVec = new THREE.Vector3();
006964:       function _cameraSpaceDistance(pos) {
006965:         _depthPriorityVec.set(pos.x, pos.y, pos.z).applyMatrix4(camera.matrixWorldInverse);

010457:       function beginNpcDialogueStaging(walker) {
010458:         // Cutscene Preview drives every participant's position/facing itself
010459:         // (see "Cutscene Preview Mode" below) — walking/turning the real
010460:         // singleton `player` to stand next to whoever it opened dialogue
010461:         // with would fight the director's own scripted blocking, and there
010462:         // may not even be a "player" in the scene the preview is running.
010463:         if (cutscenePreviewActive) return;
010464:         const npcX = walker?.root?.position?.x;
010465:         const npcZ = walker?.root?.position?.z;
010466:         if (!Number.isFinite(npcX) || !Number.isFinite(npcZ)) { npcDialogueStaging = null; return; }
010467:         const playerWorldX = player.x / TILE;
010468:         const playerWorldZ = player.y / TILE;
010469:         const candidates = npcDialogueStagingOffsets().map(offset => ({
010470:           x: npcX + (Number(offset.x) || 0),
010471:           z: npcZ + (Number(offset.y) || 0),
010472:         }));
010473:         candidates.sort((a, b) => Math.hypot(playerWorldX - a.x, playerWorldZ - a.z) - Math.hypot(playerWorldX - b.x, playerWorldZ - b.z));
010474:         const target = candidates.find(pos => canPlayerOccupy(pos.x * TILE, pos.z * TILE)) || candidates[0];
010475:         npcDialogueStaging = { walker, targetX: target.x, targetZ: target.z };
010476:         player.vx = 0;
010477:         player.vy = 0;
010478:       }
010479: 
010480:       // Continuous "eye contact" aim, ported from the Multi-Avatar Animation
010481:       // Author's actor gaze system (aimActorNeckAtTarget/actorEyeWorldPosition
010482:       // in docs/tools/animation-author/index.html — used there for e.g. the
010483:       // dance preset, where two actors of different heights still need to
010484:       // convincingly meet each other's eyes): computes yaw AND pitch together
010485:       // from the real 3D direction between two eye-height world points, then
010486:       // transforms that direction into the neck bone's own parent space, so
010487:       // the result is automatically correct regardless of how the body is
010488:       // currently rotated — unlike aiming at the residual gap against the
010489:       // body's own (slower) facing lerp, this doesn't decay back toward zero
010490:       // once the body catches up. Called every frame, it holds a steady
010491:       // "looking at you" pose for as long as it keeps being called, which is
010492:       // what a conversation needs (the gaze should persist for the whole
010493:       // exchange, not just the moment right after it opens).
010494:       function _dialogueEyeWorldPosition(rootPosition, modelHeight) {
010495:         return new THREE.Vector3(rootPosition.x, rootPosition.y + modelHeight * PLAYER_FACE_HEIGHT_RATIO, rootPosition.z);
010496:       }
010497: 
010498:       function _aimNeckAtWorldPoint(neckJoint, selfRootPosition, selfModelHeight, targetEyeWorld, maxYawDeg, maxPitchDeg, debugEntity) {
010499:         if (!neckJoint?.parent || !targetEyeWorld) return false;
010500:         neckJoint.parent.updateMatrixWorld(true);
010501:         const selfEyeWorld = _dialogueEyeWorldPosition(selfRootPosition, selfModelHeight);
010502:         if (debugEntity) debugEntity._lookAtDebug = { head: { x: selfEyeWorld.x, y: selfEyeWorld.y, z: selfEyeWorld.z }, target: { x: targetEyeWorld.x, y: targetEyeWorld.y, z: targetEyeWorld.z } };
010503:         const direction = neckJoint.parent.worldToLocal(targetEyeWorld.clone()).sub(neckJoint.parent.worldToLocal(selfEyeWorld));
010504:         const horizontal = Math.hypot(direction.x, direction.z);
010505:         if (direction.lengthSq() < 1e-8) return false;
010506:         const yawDeg = Math.max(-maxYawDeg, Math.min(maxYawDeg, Math.atan2(direction.x, direction.z) * 180 / Math.PI));
010507:         const pitchDeg = Math.max(-maxPitchDeg, Math.min(maxPitchDeg, -Math.atan2(direction.y, Math.max(.0001, horizontal)) * 180 / Math.PI));
010508:         neckJoint.rotation.set(pitchDeg * Math.PI / 180, yawDeg * Math.PI / 180, 0);
010509:         return true;
010510:       }
-----
010546:           walker.applyDialogueEyeContact(playerEyeWorld, dt, cfg);
010547:         } else if (walker.neckJoint) {
010548:           _aimNeckAtEyeContact(walker.neckJoint, walker.root.position, walker.avatarHeight, playerMesh.position, playerAvatarModelHeight, maxYawDeg, maxPitchDeg, walker);
010549:         }
010550:         if (playerNeckJoint) {
010551:           const speakerEyeWorld = typeof walker.dialogueHeadWorldPosition === 'function'
010552:             ? walker.dialogueHeadWorldPosition(new THREE.Vector3())
010553:             : _dialogueEyeWorldPosition(walker.root.position, walker.avatarHeight);
010554:           _aimNeckAtWorldPoint(playerNeckJoint, playerMesh.position, playerAvatarModelHeight, speakerEyeWorld, maxYawDeg, maxPitchDeg, player);
010555:         }
010556:       }

010558:       function updateNpcDialogueStaging(dt) {
010559:         if (cutscenePreviewActive) return; // see beginNpcDialogueStaging
010560:         if (!npcDialogueStaging?.walker?.root) return;
010561:         const cfg = npcDialogueStagingConfig();
010562:         const speed = (cfg.moveSpeedTilesPerSecond ?? 4.25) * TILE;
010563:         const arrival = (cfg.arrivalRadiusTiles ?? 0.08) * TILE;
010564:         const targetX = npcDialogueStaging.targetX * TILE;
010565:         const targetY = npcDialogueStaging.targetZ * TILE;
010566:         const dx = targetX - player.x;
010567:         const dy = targetY - player.y;
010568:         const dist = Math.hypot(dx, dy);
010569:         if (dist <= arrival) {
010570:           player.x = targetX;
010571:           player.y = targetY;
010572:           player.vx = 0;
010573:           player.vy = 0;
010574:           faceNpcDialogueParticipants(dt);
010575:           return;
010576:         }
010577:         const step = Math.min(dist, speed * dt);
010578:         const desiredX = player.x + dx / dist * step;
010579:         const desiredY = player.y + dy / dist * step;
010580:         let moved = false;
010581:         if (canPlayerOccupy(desiredX, player.y)) { player.x = desiredX; moved = true; }
010582:         if (canPlayerOccupy(player.x, desiredY)) { player.y = desiredY; moved = true; }
010583:         player.vx = moved ? dx / dist * speed : 0;
010584:         player.vy = moved ? dy / dist * speed : 0;
010585:         faceNpcDialogueParticipants(dt);
010586:       }
010587:

010595:           style: cfg.style || 'primary',
010596:           allowed: true,
010597:         };
010598:       }

018650:       // Every mesh worth pulling the camera in front of, for whatever area is

018656:       // it by tagging alone — read _zoneBuildingGroups fresh each call

018658:       // placed furniture, have no static tagged collection at all — the
018659:       // farmhouse, barn, town buildings, and furniture can all sit between
018660:       // the camera and the player (the house/barn were the reported case
018661:       // for losing sight of animals behind them; furniture matters for the
018662:       // seated camera specifically, since a chair can easily have another
018663:       // piece of furniture right behind it) — so those are gathered fresh
018664:       // each call instead. Cheap in practice: a handful of structures/
018665:       // furniture pieces at most, and this only runs once a frame.
